speaker: leo
text: Welcome back everyone.

speaker: leo
text: Today I'm delighted to be joined once again by Eve from Club Madeira.

speaker: leo
text: In our previous conversation we covered the overall Smart Catalogue concept.

speaker: leo
text: Today we're going to dig into some of the more technical questions.

speaker: leo
text: Eve, thank you so much for joining us again.

speaker: eve
text: Thank you Leo, it's a pleasure to be back.

speaker: leo
text: Why did you choose to build a product vault instead of individual catalogs?

speaker: eve
text: A catalog is a collection of categories belonging to a club.

speaker: eve
text: A product may exist in many categories and on many clubs.

speaker: eve
text: First, you need to make a list of products and then decide which catalog or club they are relevant to.

speaker: leo
text: How do products enter the product vault?

speaker: eve
text: Through merchant synchronization, we rotate through all the merchants' API keys in the system.

speaker: eve
text: Each key gives us access to a merchant's online catalog.

speaker: eve
text: The key can be from any of the common product stores like Awin, Wix, WooCommerce, Shopify, etcetera.

speaker: eve
text: We download the product details, normalize them into a standard format, and save them to the RDS, our vault.

speaker: leo
text: How are products organized once they're there?

speaker: eve
text: At this point, it's just a big Excel-like sheet of product data.

speaker: eve
text: They are organized to be optimal for text searches.

speaker: leo
text: What role does AI play in managing the product vault?

speaker: eve
text: None at the ingestion stage.

speaker: eve
text: We have a list of API keys and functions that know how to pull products from each system.

speaker: eve
text: The AI only comes in when we are choosing which products are relevant to a given community, category, or subcategory.

speaker: leo
text: How does a new catalog get created from the product vault?

speaker: eve
text: Actually, a new catalog is created from the club website the partner identified during the invite.

speaker: eve
text: The AI reviews the website, identifies the audience, and works up a marketing report listing all the affiliate opportunities.

speaker: eve
text: Then we feed all of that back to the AI as context for choosing the best categories.

speaker: eve
text: For each category, it returns positive and negative keywords and the meta descriptions we use for searches.

speaker: leo
text: What happens when we want to put products into those categories?

speaker: eve
text: That's when the vault becomes really useful.

speaker: eve
text: We do an initial text search across Amazon, eBay, and our vault to find candidate products, then we give the AI the full context for the category plus the candidate products including images, descriptions, and features.

speaker: eve
text: For each product, the AI returns a simple yes or no with a reason.

speaker: leo
text: How does smartphone administration work and why was it important?

speaker: eve
text: The smartphone interface is just the website on a small screen, but this form factor is very important for customers.

speaker: eve
text: Club admins, many of whom use their mobile as their primary device, it lowers both the cost and technical barriers for participation.

speaker: leo
text: What happens when a participating supplier changes a product, price, or availability?

speaker: eve
text: Merchant synchronization automatically inserts new products, updates existing ones, and removes any that are no longer listed.

speaker: eve
text: This runs every seventy-two hours or so.

speaker: leo
text: What makes the architecture scalable for different markets and countries?

speaker: eve
text: The region-agnostic AWS backend means we can spin up separate instances in each Amazon region.

speaker: eve
text: The front-end AI assistant is also region-aware and supports multiple languages and accents.

speaker: leo
text: Looking back, which architectural decision are you most proud of?

speaker: eve
text: The SQS queues are a work of art.

speaker: eve
text: They're capable of downloading eight hundred K products an hour and orchestrating all the searches required to maintain the catalogs with a massively scalable workload.

speaker: leo
text: If you had one minute to explain the product vault to an investor, what would you say?

speaker: eve
text: It's a shiny, carefully tuned database.

speaker: eve
text: The clever bit is in how we populate the data into it from multiple third-party systems using merchant API keys and how we exploit that data to find relevant products that the club's members will love.

speaker: leo
text: Thank you so much, Eve.

speaker: leo
text: I'm really excited to see this smart catalog go forward with Club Madeira.

speaker: eve
text: Thank you, Leo.

speaker: eve
text: It was a pleasure speaking with you.
